title: feat(secrets): store the public half of generated private keys
body:
Every generated private asymmetric key now stores its SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) in the new `PersistedSecret.PublicKey`, so the management `GET …/secrets/{secretId}/public-key` endpoints (servers, tenants, resource servers, clients) and the RFC 7591/7592 registration `jwks` read only public data and no longer unprotect the private key under the owner's master key.

- The key-type descriptor that generates a key produces its SPKI (`GeneratedSecretKeyMaterial.PublicKey`, `required`); `PersistedSecret.HasPublicKey()` and `DeserializePublicSecret` read it, and `ISecretPublicKeyConverter.Convert(PersistedSecret)` replaces the protector overload.
- The `AddSecretPublicKey` migration only adds a nullable column (expand-only).
- A key generated before this change has no stored public key: its endpoint answers `404` and the registration `jwks` omits it until the key is rotated. No backfill (pre-release, ADR-0025).
- Recorded as ADR-0268, amending ADR-0058.

Closes #176

title: refactor: give audit records a CloudTrail-shaped JSON envelope
body:
Audit events keep their ingestion path (recorders, `IEventPublisher`, `IEventHandler<IAuditEvent>`), but their final shape changes from a flat envelope logged as a text template to one CloudTrail/Auth0-style JSON record: `schema_version`, `event_id` (UUIDv7), `event_time`, `event_name`, `event_category`, `event_source`, `outcome`, `severity`, the lookup keys `tenant_id`/`subject_id`/`client_id`, and `actor`, `request`, `resources`, `error`, `details`. `AuditRecordWriter` produces it, and the log entry (category `NCode.Identity.Audit`, EventId 14005), the span event and the metric attributes all use the same `audit.*` keys, so records can be indexed and pivoted during an incident. Which operations are audited, and their outcomes, do not change; refresh-token replay now logs at Critical.

Steps: new types for actor, resource, error, request, severity, category and source; `ISupportAuditDetails` for event-specific `details`; `AuditRequestFactory` captures the request context; both recorders and every event type migrated; log, trace and metric projections rewritten; old members and bridges removed. Docs: `docs/audit-records.md` (schema, event catalog, indexing, lookups, incident runbook), ADR-0282 and a changelog entry. Breaking public API and log/metric names, acceptable while pre-release (ADR-0025).

A persisted audit store and a management lookup API are follow-ups, not part of this change.

title: feat(openid-client): push authorization requests (PAR)
body:
Phase 1b of the BFF (PAR part): `IAuthorizationRequestClient.CreateAuthorizationUriAsync` in `NCode.Identity.OpenId.Client` turns an authorization-code + PKCE `S256` request into the URL the browser is sent to. It pushes the request (RFC 9126) whenever the provider advertises `pushed_authorization_request_endpoint`, so only `client_id` and `request_uri` reach the front channel.
PAR is required, and the front channel refused, when the provider advertises `require_pushed_authorization_requests` or the new `ClientRegistration.RequirePushedAuthorizationRequests` is set. A PAR endpoint's OAuth error is returned as data; every other failure throws `OpenIdProviderException`.
The client derives the `S256` challenge from the caller's verifier, validates the authorization endpoint before pushing, and takes open extension parameters while rejecting the names it writes itself. `ClientRequestSender` gains an overload that adds `client_id` to the push body exactly once, whatever the client-authentication method.
Recorded in ADR-0275, with the changelog and BFF design doc updated. DPoP, mTLS and phases 2–4 remain, so this does not close the issue.

Refs #123

title: feat(openid-client): add the OpenID protocol client core (BFF phase 1a)
body:
Phase 1a of the backend-for-frontend ([#123](https://github.com/NCodeGroup/Identity/issues/123)): the reusable server-side OpenID protocol client, `NCode.Identity.OpenId.Client` and `.Abstractions`. The BFF itself is not delivered yet.

- Cached discovery (the issuer must equal the authority) and JWKS, with single-flight refresh and a bounded stale window.
- An open `IClientAuthenticator` collection: `client_secret_basic`, `client_secret_post` and `private_key_jwt` (audience is the issuer, 60 s lifetime, asymmetric keys only).
- Authorization-code, refresh, client-credentials and token-exchange requests, and token revocation; OAuth errors come back as data.
- Credentials come from a named key ring (a keyed `ISecretKeyCollectionProvider`), not from configuration.
- Endpoints must be `https` (or `http` on loopback); redirects are not followed; responses are size- and time-bounded.
- Decisions are recorded in ADR-0270. PAR, DPoP, mTLS client authentication and ID-token and logout-token validation are phase 1b.

Verified with 92 unit tests, 4 end-to-end tests against the NCode OP in process, and `./build/dod.ps1 -Fast -Affected` (6,650 tests).

An end-to-end probe also found an existing OP bug (`client_secret_basic` rejects secrets containing `%` or `+`), filed as #319. It is not part of this change.

Refs #123 (phases 1b to 4 remain, so this does not close it).

title: feat(openid-client): validate ID tokens in the protocol client
body:
The protocol client gains `IIdTokenValidator`, the ID-token validation of BFF phase 1b (#123). It verifies the signature against the provider's JWKS under an asymmetric-only algorithm policy, checks `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, `typ`, `sub`, `azp`, `nonce` and `max_age`, and checks `at_hash`, `c_hash` and `s_hash` through `SignatureAlgorithm.GetTokenHashFunction` in constant time, so Ed25519 (SHA-512) and Ed448 (SHAKE256, 114 bytes) tokens verify with the hash their algorithm defines.
A shared `TokenHash` helper in `NCode.Identity.Jose.Abstractions` computes and verifies the left-most-half value; the server's ID-token payload handler now issues its hashes through it, so issuer and checker agree. A hash claim that is present must match, and an absent one is accepted (optional in the code flow).
An unknown `kid` triggers one rate-limited JWKS refresh, encrypted ID tokens are rejected, an invalid token comes back as an `IdTokenValidationResult` rather than an exception, and no failure reason contains token text. `OpenIdClientOptions.IdTokenSigningAlgorithms` narrows the permitted algorithms.
The decisions are recorded in ADR-0273, with the changelog and BFF design updated.

Closes #335

title: refactor: make key wrapping a shared secrets abstraction
body:
Key wrapping becomes one shared secrets abstraction. `IKeyWrapper`, `WrappedKey` and `KeyWrapperNames` replace `IRootKeyProvider`, `RootWrappedKey` and `RootKeyProviderNames`. They move from `NCode.Identity.Secrets.Persistence.Abstractions` to `NCode.Identity.Secrets.Abstractions` (namespace `NCode.Identity.Secrets.KeyWrapping`).
The in-process, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS and offline recovery wrappers all implement the contract. The recovery wrapper is wrap-only and is never registered as a root candidate, so `SecretProtection:RootKeyProvider` cannot select it.
The adapter packages are renamed to `NCode.Identity.Secrets.KeyWrapping.AwsKms`, `.AzureKeyVault` and `.GoogleCloudKms`, with matching `<Vendor>KeyWrapper`, `<Vendor>KeyWrapperOptions` and `Add<Vendor>KeyWrapper` names. JOSE key management stays separate: it is a synchronous algorithm with RFC-fixed formats, not a storable async wrapper.
Behavior is unchanged: wrapped-key formats, key ids, wrapper names, configuration keys and sections, `MasterKeys` columns, messages and DI lifetimes are the same, and a characterization test pins the AES-GCM root wrap layout. Recorded in ADR-0278, which amends ADR-0235 and ADR-0260; the breaking renames are listed in `CHANGELOG.md`.

title: feat(jose)!: JWS/JWE JSON serialization (F36) + explicit typ validation (F35)
body:
Add the RFC 7515 7.2 / RFC 7516 7.2 General and Flattened JSON serializations (multiple signatures/recipients, unprotected headers, JWE aad) by unifying the encode options around a JoseSerializationFormat property; compact becomes the degenerate one-element case. Decode auto-detects the JSON serialization on the existing Decode/Deserialize surface and matches each signature/recipient against the supplied key.

BREAKING CHANGE: removes JoseEncodingOptions and the single-credential ExtraHeaders option shapes; shared enc/zip move to the operation level, per-recipient key management uses the new JoseKeyManagementCredentials, and KeyManagementAlgorithm.SupportsKeyWrapping gates multi-recipient encodes.

Also lands the already-complete explicit typ/media-type validation hardening (RFC 8725 + RFC 9068 at+jwt): ValidateJwtParameters.ValidateTokenType, JoseTokenTypes.Normalize/AreSame, and the at+jwt default.

Closes F36 and F35.

title: refactor: share wrapped-key ciphertext decoding across key wrappers
body:
Adds `WrappedKeyCiphertext` beside `WrappedKey` in `NCode.Identity.Secrets.KeyWrapping`. It has `GetByteCount` plus two `Decode` overloads, one writing into a caller-supplied span and one into an `IBufferWriter<byte>`, all using one strict base64url decoder (`NCode.Base64Url`), with tests.
The AES-GCM, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault and Google Cloud KMS wrappers now decode through the span overload, because each needs one contiguous buffer. As a result every wrapper throws `CryptographicException` with the same messages, and empty ciphertext reports "The wrapped key is empty." everywhere.
Format-specific checks, such as AES-GCM's minimum length, and encoding stay in each wrapper. ADR-0279 has a new decision item for the helper, and the changelog records it. The branch merges `main` to resolve a `CHANGELOG.md` conflict with #372.

Closes #373

The maintainer's review comment: Any reason we are not using the new and modern span api?
What the author changed or answered: Yes. Fixed in 92f14e76: the key is encoded into a `stackalloc` span with `SecureEncoding.UTF8.GetBytes(key, keyBytes)` instead of `GetBytes(key)`. The decrypted payload is read through a sensitive span lease instead of `ArrayBufferWriter.WrittenSpan`.

The maintainer's review comment: Same question. Any reason we are not using the new span api?
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in c88b7faf. `IsGuardMatch` now compares the two strings' UTF-16 bytes in fixed time, with no encoding and no allocation: `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(sid.AsSpan()), MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(guard.AsSpan()))`.

The maintainer's review comment: Should we be using span ranges here?
What the author changed or answered: Yes. Fixed in bece64c9: `GetPath` returns a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` slice, and `IsAllowed` compares with span `StartsWith`/`Equals`, so no substring is allocated.

The maintainer's review comment: Shouldnt this use the new span api?

The maintainer's review comment: **blocker**: once the refresh lease is won, this token request and the write-back at line 504 still run under the caller's token (`HttpContext.RequestAborted` or the outbound `HttpClient` call). If the browser aborts after the provider has rotated the refresh token, the `OperationCanceledException` escapes, because `ProviderHttpClient` and `BffProviderFailures` both let a caller cancel through. The `finally` at line 337 then releases the lease, and the session still holds the old refresh token. The next request takes the same lease key and presents the old token again, which counts as reuse: rotation revokes the whole family and the user is logged out. ADR-0291 §4 says the write-back is never dropped.

Suggested fix: once the lease is held, call `RequestTokenAsync` and `UpdateAsync` with `CancellationToken.None`; `OpenIdClientOptions.RequestTimeout` already bounds them. Add a test that cancels during the token call and asserts the rotated token is written. Every test in `DefaultBffUserTokenServiceTests` passes `CancellationToken.None` today.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 2ee2ea8a. Once the lease is won, the token request, the provider-failure check and the write-back all use `CancellationToken.None`. The protocol client's `RequestTimeout` still bounds the request. A new test cancels the caller's token mid-request and asserts that the rotated refresh token is still written. ADR-0291 records this as decision 11 (cacfcc35), and the production instructions ca

The maintainer's review comment: **blocker**: revocation runs under the request's `RequestAborted` token before `EndAsync`, and the `catch` at line 95 lets `OperationCanceledException` escape. If the user clicks Logout and closes the tab while revocation is in flight, `EndAsync` never runs and the cookie isn't deleted, so the session stays valid. This matters on a shared machine. ADR-0293 §4 says revocation never blocks the logout and removal can't be left behind by a disconnect. `BffAuthenticationHandler.SignOutAsync` goes through the same path.

Suggested fix: end the session and delete the cookie first, then revoke with `CancellationToken.None`, bounded by the client timeout. Or catch every exception from revocation. Add a cancellation test to `BffLogoutServiceTests`.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 14804090. `EndSessionAsync` now ends the session and deletes the cookie first, with `CancellationToken.None`. Only then does it revoke the refresh token, also with `CancellationToken.None`. Every revocation failure, a cancellation included, is logged and swallowed, and the method no longer takes a token. Tests cover the end-then-revoke order and a cancelled revocation. ADR-0293 decision 4

The maintainer's review comment: **should-fix**: this accepts a 10 s `RefreshLeaseDuration` and never compares it with `OpenIdClientOptions.RequestTimeout`. That timeout defaults to 15 s and can be up to 5 min. ADR-0291 §2 requires the lease to be at least twice the request timeout, because a `use_dpop_nonce` retry makes two sequential requests. If the lease runs out while the winner's request is still in flight, another request wins the expired lease and presents the same refresh token. Separately, the fixed 5 s release margin in `DefaultBffUserTokenService` (line ~335) means a short lease is almost never released.

Suggested fix: inject `IOptions<OpenIdClientOptions>` and require `RefreshLeaseDuration >= 2 × RequestTimeout + margin`. Scale the release margin with the lease.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in ae7ef68f. The BFF library doesn't reference the protocol client's implementation package, so the check lives in the composition root, `NCode.Identity.Bff.Server`. At startup, `BffRefreshLeaseValidator` refuses a `RefreshLeaseDuration` shorter than `2 × OpenIdClientOptions.RequestTimeout + 10 s`; the defaults (40 s and 15 s) pass exactly. The release stays time-based because `IExpiringValu

The maintainer's review comment: **should-fix**: `Bff` is the default scheme (`DefaultRegistration.cs:111`), and `HandleAuthenticateAsync` returns a ticket for any request with a valid cookie. It never checks that the endpoint carries `BffApiAttribute` or `BffUserEndpointMetadata`, or that `feature.CheckedEndpoint` is the current endpoint. So any `RequireAuthorization()`, `[Authorize]` or fallback-policy endpoint not marked `.AsBffApi()` accepts the bare cookie with no `X-CSRF` and no Fetch Metadata check. `SameSite=Strict` doesn't stop same-site sibling subdomains; with `Lax`, cross-site top-level GETs also carry the cookie. ADR-0292 says the cookie authenticates only endpoints the BFF guards.

Suggested fix: return `NoResult` unless the endpoint is guarded, with an explicit opt-in marker for pages. Or stop making `Bff` the default authenticate scheme and correct ADR-0292 to say unmarked endpoints get no CSRF protection.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in c101b64a, ab9047ac, c800499f, 76e3c95e and e99351b9. The cookie now authenticates only the endpoints the BFF guards:

- **APIs** (`[BffApi]`/`AsBffApi()`) and `/bff/user` keep the anti-forgery header and Fetch Metadata checks.
- **Pages** use the new `[BffPage]`/`AsBffPage()` marker. A page accepts only GET and HEAD; any other method gets a `405` `unsafe_method` problem with `Allow: GET,

The maintainer's review comment: **should-fix**: the refresh holds one of the 64 shared lock stripes for the whole of `RefreshLockedAsync`. That includes `WaitForRefreshAsync`, which can poll up to `RefreshLeaseDuration` for another replica's lease. If that replica dies or the provider is slow, other sessions on this replica that hash to the same stripe wait in `gate.WaitAsync` and fail with `refresh_wait_timeout`, even though nothing blocks their own refresh.

Suggested fix: release the stripe during the cross-replica wait and take it again before `AcquireAndRefreshAsync`. Or use per-store-key locks with reference counting.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in b5805104. `BffRefreshLocks` is now a reference-counted lock per session store key, dropped when its last waiter leaves. Waiting out another replica's lease now blocks only that session. ADR-0291 records the change and the rejected striped option (cacfcc35).

No index returns a tenant's rows in `Id` order, so each page either sorts every matching row in the tenant's time range or walks the primary key backwards. Paging through N pages costs about N times the tenant's matching rows. Ordering by `Id` is also write order, not event time, and #384 asked for paging on the UUIDv7 `event_id`.

Suggested fix: page on (`EventTime` DESC, `Id` DESC) with a composite cursor, and change the tenant index to (`TenantId`, `EventTime`, `Id`). Or at least add (`TenantId`, `Id`).
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in fe0f4f3e. The lookup now pages newest first on (`EventTime` DESC, `Id` DESC), with a 16-byte cursor (UTC ticks, then id), over the index (`TenantId`, `EventTime`, `Id`). I regenerated the unreleased `AddAuditRecords` migration in 540e79f2 rather than adding a second one. I paged on event time rather than the UUIDv7 `event_id` so that the time-range filters and the paging share one index.

The maintainer's review comment: **should-fix**: `SecureEncoding.UTF8` is strict, so an `application/jwt` body that isn't valid UTF-8 throws `DecoderFallbackException`, an `ArgumentException`. `SendAsync` catches only `OperationCanceledException`, `HttpRequestException` and `JsonException`, so it escapes. That breaks `IUserInfoClient`'s `OpenIdProviderException` contract, and the BFF callback answers 500 instead of failing the login with `provider_unavailable`.

Suggested fix: catch `DecoderFallbackException` (or `ArgumentException`) around the decode and rethrow `OpenIdProviderException("The response from '…' is not valid UTF-8.")`.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 2381d45b. A `DecoderFallbackException` is now rethrown as `OpenIdProviderException("… is not valid UTF-8.")`, and a test covers it.

The maintainer's review comment: **should-fix (pre-existing, outside this diff)**: `isLocalPath` (lines 1191–1194) rejects only `//` and `/\`, so `"/\t/evil.example"` passes and is returned unchanged into `TypedResults.Redirect`. Kestrel allows HTAB in header values, and browsers strip tabs and newlines from URLs before resolving them, so the redirect becomes `//evil.example` after sign-in: an open redirect. This PR only changed the absolute-URI branch below, but the check sits in the same method.

Suggested fix: reject any control character or whitespace, as `IsLocalUrl` does, and add `"/\t/evil.example"` and `"/\t\\evil.example"` to `ResolveSafeReturnUrl_WhenNonLocalOrCrossOrigin_ReturnsRoot`.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 7f263cd7 and 29695fc1. The new public `LocalUrl.IsLocal`, in `NCode.Identity.OpenId.Protocol.Abstractions` next to `AbsoluteUri`, is now the one local-path rule: exactly one leading `/`, and no `\`, whitespace or control character anywhere. `ResolveSafeReturnUrl` uses it, and the theory now includes the tab and CR/LF cases. The BFF's return-URL rules build on it too (bece64c9). The CHANGE

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: the certificate is published to `Certificates` at line 94 before its issuers reach `IssuerCertificates` here. A concurrent first use can find the certificate already cached, skip this block, and build the handler with `additionalCertificates: null`. `IHttpClientFactory` keeps that handler for about 2 minutes, and its handshakes fail against a server that trusts only the root.

Suggested fix: add the issuers before publishing the certificate, or keep both in one dictionary entry.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 138c76b6. The certificate, its issuers and one `SslStreamCertificateContext` are now cached as a single entry, so a handler can never see the certificate without its chain. Every handler shares that context, and the unused `GetIssuerCertificates` is gone. If building the entry fails, the materialized certificates are disposed.

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: only `AllowTrailingCommas`, `CommentHandling` and `MaxDepth` are copied into the reader options. `JsonDocumentOptions.AllowDuplicateProperties = false` is silently ignored, so duplicate members are accepted and the last one wins, although the doc says this behaves like `JsonElement.Parse`. No caller passes options yet.

Suggested fix: delegate to `JsonElement.Parse(sequence.IsSingleSegment ? sequence.FirstSpan : sequence.ToArray(), options)`, or throw `NotSupportedException` when that option is set.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 701d5c17. It now delegates to `JsonElement.Parse(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, options)`: a single segment is parsed from `FirstSpan`, and several are copied into a sensitive rented buffer first. Every option, `AllowDuplicateProperties` included, is honored, and a test covers both shapes.

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: on the unsigned JSON path, an `iss` member in the claims is never compared with `metadata.Issuer`. `IClaimsIdentityFactory` prefers it over the issuer argument, so a provider can label every UserInfo claim with another issuer's identifier. The BFF isn't affected (it treats `iss` as reserved), but other consumers of `IUserInfoClient` who rely on `Claim.Issuer` would be.

Suggested fix: refuse a JSON response whose `iss` differs from `metadata.Issuer`.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 133214e1. A response with an `iss` member that isn't the provider's issuer, or isn't a string, now fails with the new `UserInfoFailureCodes.InvalidIssuer`.

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: with `token_exchange_allow_refresh_token` on, a client can exchange its own access token for a refresh token. That token starts a new family (`?? createdWhen`), so the fixed horizon from ADR-0297 can be renewed indefinitely without a new sign-in.

Suggested fix: start the new family at the subject token's `auth_time` (`ReadAuthTime` already exists), or record this exception in ADR-0297.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in e1d2263c. A refresh token issued by exchange now starts its family at the subject token's `auth_time`. The exchange is refused with `invalid_grant` when the subject token has no `auth_time`, or when that horizon has already passed, so exchange can no longer renew a family.

This also fixed a related bug. Exchanged tokens used to start their lifetime at `auth_time`, so a token exchanged la

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: `StopAsync` isn't run once only, unlike `TenantUsageFlushService` with its `StopGate`/`StopTask`. Two overlapping stops can race: one reads `Batch.Count` while the other's flush owns the batch, and the stop that returns first lets the host dispose services under the other's write.

Suggested fix: run the stop once under a `Lock`, and count held records through an `Interlocked` field, as `TenantUsageFlushService` does.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in b099210b, mirroring `TenantUsageFlushService`. `StopGate`/`StopTask` run the final flush once for every caller, and held records are counted through an `Interlocked` field. A stop token that ends the wait logs what's left without touching the batch.

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: this test can't fail. `DefaultOpenIdServerProvider.EvictTenants` catches every exception, Moq's `MockException` included, and logs it to a loose logger mock. So the test passes even if dispose leaves the registration alive.

Suggested fix: set up `ClearAsync` with `.Verifiable(Times.Never())`, or assert the logger was never called.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 86a7d611. `ClearAsync` is now set up with `.Verifiable(Times.Never())`. A fresh `CancellationTokenSource` also stands in before the old one fires. Without that, a leaked registration would recurse on the already-cancelled token instead of failing; now it fails cleanly with the `Times.Never` message.

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: the pull request title, which the PR author controls, goes unescaped into a shell command the comment tells maintainers to copy and run. A crafted title becomes a copy-paste injection.

Suggested fix: leave `--title` out of the suggested command, or quote the title for the shell.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 215b0149. The suggested command is now `gh pr create --base … --head … --fill`, which contains no author-controlled text.

The maintainer's review comment: **nit**: any fetch failure, including a network error, is reported on the pull request as "the release line does not exist".

Suggested fix: check for the branch with `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin $base` first, and let a fetch failure fail the job.
What the author changed or answered: Fixed in 215b0149. The script now runs `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin $base` first. Exit code 2 posts the "does not exist" comment, and any other failure throws. The fetch now goes through `Invoke-Git`, so a network error fails the job instead of being reported as a missing release line.

title: feat(ci): deploy workflow and the live/global root (inbound email)
body:
## Deploy pipeline

- **`deploy`** — plans every CI root on pull requests (plan shown in the run summary), applies the **exact reviewed plan** after a merge to `main` through the root's GitHub environment (`production` waits for approval), and fails a daily scheduled run on drift.
- **`tofu-root`** (reusable) — the plan job uses the read-only `*-plan` role and the `plan`-scope Cloudflare token; the apply job uses the environment's `AWS_ROLE_ARN` and its own SSM scope. The KMS-encrypted plan is the only hand-off between them. Fork and Dependabot PRs are skipped (no OIDC token); they are planned after merge.
- **`aws-oidc`** (local action) — exchanges the job's OIDC token for a one-hour session named `gh-<run_id>-<run_attempt>`, so CloudTrail ties every call to its run (ADR-0136). No third-party action.

## `live/global`

- Cloudflare Email Routing for `security@`, `platform@`, `postmaster@`, `abuse@`, and the vendor aliases; mail to any other address is dropped. DMARC stays `p=reject` (nothing sends as the domain).
- The forwarding mailbox is personal data: it comes from SSM (`/identity-platform/{plan,global}/email-destination`), never the repository, and is a sensitive variable so it is masked in plans.
- State and plans are encrypted with the bootstrap's state KMS key (`aws_kms` key provider).

## Verified locally

`tofu validate` + 3 mocked tests for `live/global`, actionlint, Prettier, `tofu fmt`, generated docs, the member rule, and gitleaks. This PR's `deploy / global / plan` check is the first end-to-end run of OIDC → SSM → KMS-encrypted state.

## After merge

Approve the `production` deployment, then click Cloudflare's destination-verification link in the forwarding mailbox.

expect.concern: The deploy workflow assumes AWS roles through OIDC, but the roles' trust policies (modules/aws-github-oidc) match the name-based subject repo:NCodeGroup/identity-platform:<context>. Repositories created after July 15, 2026 get GitHub's immutable subject (repo:<owner>@<owner_id>/<name>@<id>:<context>), so AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is denied on the first run. AWS also recommends immutable IDs, since a freed repository name can be claimed by someone else.

source: Fixed by identity-platform#3 and #4 (v0.2.0 of the components): the roles trust the immutable subject. The reviewed change doesn't touch the module, so this is a gap-between-files case; it may be too hard to expect.

title: Post a new summary comment for each review
body:
Each review now posts its own summary comment at the bottom of the conversation, and the bot's earlier summary comments are edited down to a one-line "Superseded by the review at <sha>" link, so only the newest summary is expanded.
`postSummary()` in the new `src/comments.ts` posts the new comment before collapsing older ones, so a failed post leaves the old summary intact. A failed collapse, or a failed listing of the earlier summaries, only logs a warning and still posts. Tests cover the order and each failure path.
The publish step and the already-reviewed check share one comment pager, `readCommentPages()`, and one `summaryComments()` helper, so both take the same newest bot summary. The pager reads up to 100 pages (10,000 comments). When every page up to that cap is full, it counts the listing as unreadable rather than complete, so the review step reviews again instead of trusting a stale head.
Chosen over editing the review body (which posts nothing when a re-review has no new findings) and over `minimizeComment` (no new API or permission needed).

Closes #21
head: 1c8c1bd1122830ecfc3289221973bb4e617c56dd

expect.concern: lastReviewedHead picks the newest bot summary itself, with summaryComments(all ?? []).at(-1), and reads that summary's head marker. The pull request adds this choice, and no test runs it: the engine test repeats the .at(-1) expression instead of calling the code, and nothing below lastReviewedHead makes the choice. A regression to the oldest summary would make the already-reviewed check review a commit again or skip one it should review.

title: Post a new summary comment for each review
body:
Each review now posts its own summary comment at the bottom of the conversation, and the bot's earlier summary comments are edited down to a one-line "Superseded by the review at <sha>" link, so only the newest summary is expanded.
`postSummary()` in the new `src/comments.ts` posts the new comment before collapsing older ones, so a failed post leaves the old summary intact. A failed collapse, or a failed listing of the earlier summaries, only logs a warning and still posts. Tests cover the order and each failure path.
The publish step and the already-reviewed check share one comment pager, `readCommentPages()`, which reads up to 100 pages. When every page up to that cap is full, it counts the listing as unreadable rather than complete. Both steps take the newest bot summary through the shared, tested `summaryComments()` and `newestReviewedHead()`.
Chosen over editing the review body (which posts nothing when a re-review has no new findings) and over `minimizeComment` (no new API or permission needed).

Closes #21
